screen-title.purpose: Screen titles only -- 'Your path', '9,738 entries', 'Your Kabiyè'. 600, 40px, 1.0, -0.02em.

step-question.purpose: What a lesson step is asking. 500, 26px, 1.15.

body.purpose: Lesson prose, definitions, all running interface copy. 400, 17px, 1.5. Always ink, never laterite.

body-small.purpose: Captions, pronunciations, glosses, secondary metadata. 400, 15px, quiet ink.

kabiye-hero.purpose: A single letter, never a word. Andika Bold 150px, 0.85.

kabiye-word.purpose: Headwords and the word being taught. Andika Bold 44px, 1.05; a word never exceeds 44 and must be allowed to wrap.

narrative.overview: A well-made teaching book that happens to be a phone. The page is calm and the word is the hero: bone paper, ink, and the red earth of Kara kept for the places where the reader acts and for the letters French cannot write. Nothing decorative competes with the language itself, because for a large part of this audience the letterforms *are* the lesson -- they are learning to read ɖ, ɛ, ɣ, ɩ, ɔ and ʋ for the first time. The system is deliberately quiet: one accent, no gradients, no shadows, no illustration. Its only real ornament is the type, because the interface speaks one voice and the Kabiyè language speaks another, and that distinction does more identity work than any decoration could. Density is generous rather than efficient -- this is a primer to sit with, not a dashboard to scan. Dark mode is a genuine second theme rather than an inversion: ink becomes the ground and laterite lifts to #E07A55 so it keeps its authority against it.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, used only where the reader acts or where the language is Kabiyè
Two typefaces with one job each: Bricolage Grotesque for the interface, Andika for Kabiyè
Flat by tone -- no shadows anywhere in the system
Generous vertical rhythm; the Kabiyè word is always the largest thing in its block
Fully paired light and dark palettes, both first-class

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one accent -- laterite -- and it means 'act here' or 'this is Kabiyè'. If a new colour seems necessary, the answer is a tonal step or a border, not a new hue.

rules.name: The Ink Button Rule
rules.body: The filled button is ink, not the accent. Laterite is spent on the hero glyph, the section label and the one primary action per screen; a screen full of laterite buttons spends it on nothing.

rules.name: The Laterite Size Floor
rules.body: Laterite passes 4.5:1 on paper only at >= 24px, or bold >= 19px. Body text is therefore always ink and never laterite.

rules.name: The Feedback-Only Rule
rules.body: There is no green and no red. Correct fills with ink; wrong is a laterite strikethrough with the correct answer beneath and an explanation. A learner should not have to know a colour code to read their own mistake.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Every Kabiyè string is Andika and every interface string is Bricolage Grotesque. The interface face draws only 4 of the 16 letters Kabiyè needs, so a Kabiyè word set in it splits across two typefaces mid-grapheme. utils/kabiye-script.ts routes this and __tests__/kabiye-font-coverage.test.ts reads the shipped binaries and fails if the next face moves the line.

rules.name: The Ink Screen Rule
rules.body: Screens that are ink from edge to edge use surface-ink / on-surface-ink, not bg-foreground / text-background. The latter swap with the theme, so an ink screen built from them inverts into a bright paper screen the moment the app goes dark.

dos: Do set every Kabiyè string in Andika, and add `kabiye` to the Text explicitly wherever the field is known to be Kabiyè.
Do separate surfaces with the tonal steps (recessed -> paper -> leaf) or with a border.
Do reserve laterite for the hero glyph, section labels, the one primary action per screen, and the Kabiyè letters French cannot write.
Do fill the primary button with ink, and use the inverse button on an ink screen.
Do let a Kabiyè word wrap rather than shrink; 44px is the ceiling, not a target.
Do pair every colour you add across both themes at once.
donts: Don't add a box-shadow. There are none, and one would be conspicuous.
Don't introduce a second accent hue. Reach for a tonal step or a border instead.
Don't use green or red for anything, including answer feedback.
Don't set body text in laterite -- it fails contrast below 24px, or bold 19px.
Don't hardcode a colour that differs between themes; use the semantic token.
Don't give letter *type* (grapheme / vowel / consonant / indication) its own colours; the label under each tile already makes that distinction.
